subject: MAP: POC environment setup — network / SSO / KMS dependencies and owners
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@gridlytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC environment setup — network / SSO / KMS dependencies and owners

Hi Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed MAP milestone owners for the POC environment setup so we can lock the target test window the week of July 19. I attached a lightweight MAP draft (MAP-draft-GridLytics-20270629.xlsx) and included the immediate technical dependencies below. Please confirm owners/timing on your side and any missing constraints.

Summary (POC environment setup) — target complete by 2027-07-16:
- VPC peering (GridLytics AWS account <-> Redwood VPC) — owner: GridLytics network team (Alex) — deliverable: peering connection + route table updates; target: 2027-07-08.
- IP allowlist for control plane + inference egress — owner: GridLytics security (Alex) — deliverable: CSV of public egress IPs / scheduled change window; target: 2027-07-10.
- SSO / SAML integration for admin console access — owner: GridLytics IdP team (Alex) + Redwood SRE (Soojin) — deliverable: SAML metadata exchange, test user, and attribute map; target: 2027-07-12.
- Secrets / KMS access pattern — owner: Redwood & GridLytics (joint) — deliverable: KMS key ARNs and cross-account IAM role or KMS grant document; target: 2027-07-14.

Open technical notes from call (action items for our side):
- Soojin: I asked you to validate whether we need a cross-account KMS grant vs. a symmetric key copy for the POC.
- Karthik: please confirm whether IP allowlist will block streaming test traffic or only control-plane API calls (we need streaming tokens unblocked).

Request for Alex: can you share your SAML metadata XML and the network team’s internal maintenance windows? If possible attach to the MAP draft on Drive (link above) or reply with the files.

Next steps:
1) Alex confirms owners/timelines (by EOD Wed 2027-06-30).
2) Redwood schedules a 30-min technical sync (Soojin + infra owner) the week of 2027-07-05 to validate peering config and test accounts.
3) We lock the POC test window for July 19–23 and finalise canary dataset for performance checks.

Thanks — Rafael

--

Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment setup — network / SSO / KMS dependencies and owners

Thanks Rafael — a few technical clarifications from the runtime side so everyone has the right expectations. I calked these into the MAP spreadsheet as well (tab: "Tech Notes"). Highlights: 

- KMS: For the POC we can proceed either with (A) a cross-account KMS grant from GridLytics KMS to a Redwood service role (preferred for auditability), or (B) a simple secrets exchange where GridLytics uploads model encryption keys to a Redwood-managed key under a short-lived agreement. Option A requires an IAM role and a KMS key policy update (we can provide a template). If GridLytics prefers Option B we need to confirm rotation/ttl.

- SAML: We will need the IdP metadata XML (cert thumbprint, entityID) and a test SSO user in the GridLytics staging directory. Attribute map we expect: email -> NameID, groups -> role. If you have a SAML test endpoint (HTTP-Redirect/POST), paste it into the Drive doc.

- IP allowlist: For streaming inference we use control-plane TLS for session negotiation and then open outbound connections for tokenized streaming over TLS to our inference pool. Practically that means you must allow our public control IPs plus a set of ephemeral egress IPs for the inference workers. I attached a csv (network-allowlist-template.csv) in the Drive; Alex — please populate with your firewall ticket ID or internal change window.

- VPC peering: note that peering is unidirectional for route tables; we will provide the CIDR ranges we need reachable (listed in the MAP draft). If you require tunnels rather than peering for policy reasons, flag that now — we may need an additional NAT/proxy.

I'll draft the KMS policy and a SAML attribute map skeleton and drop into the Drive by EOD today.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: network-allowlist-template.csv, saml-attribute-map-template.txt

Rafael / Soojin — thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick notes from GridLytics: 

- Owners: confirmed — network (me), IdP (Priya Singh), platform security (Marcus Chen). I'll loop Priya and Marcus into the Drive doc once I have the files.
- SAML metadata: attaching saml-metadata-gridlytics.xml to this thread (versioned).
- IP allowlist: we generally can schedule a maintenance window on 2027-07-09 (overnight) or 2027-07-11. 07-09 preferred. We'll populate the allowlist csv and include the firewall change request ID.
- KMS: Marcus prefers Option A (cross-account grant). He asked whether Redwood can provide an example key policy and minimal IAM role.

One ask from our infra team: can Redwood confirm whether the POC streaming will require NAT from our side or if Redwood's inference workers initiate outbound TLS to a Redwood-managed endpoint? We need to avoid opening a broad egress rule.

I can make the internal owners available on a 30-min call on Mon 2027-07-05 10:00 PT — does that work for Redwood?

Thanks — Alex
